chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about the major ritual bath (ghusl) for sexual impurity, how much water suffices? So he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to bathe with five handfuls between him and his companion (wife), and they would both bathe from one vessel.

key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: Major ritual bath for sexual impurity

ai.seo_question: How much water is required for the major ritual bath (ghusl) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the minimum water volume for ghusl al-janabah by citing the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) practice of sharing five handfuls (amdād) with his wife from a single vessel. It highlights the flexibility in ritual purity laws, demonstrating that sufficiency is determined by the washing of the entire body rather than a fixed absolute quantity, a principle highly valued in Shia fiqh for practical ease.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husay, from Safwan, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘

I asked himasws about the major Ablution (Wudhu) (for sexual impurity), how much of the water would suffice?’ So heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww used to wash with five handfuls between himsaww and hissaww companion (wife), and they would both be washing from one vessel’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from ‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah or abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about how much water is needed for Ghusl (bath) because of sexual relations. He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah would use five handfuls of water, share it with his partner, and both of them would take Ghusl (bath) from the same water container.’”
